hints.title: Deriving a New Column from Existing Attributes
hints.text: Employee compensation is stored in a salary attribute. How can you calculate a doubled compensation amount for every row and attach the result as a new column labeled bonus?

hints.title: Vectorized Arithmetic Assignment Invariant
hints.text: Arithmetic operations on pandas Series operate element-wise in C without Python loop overhead, allowing direct assignment to new column names.

hints.title: Vectorized Column Creation Procedure
hints.text: Assign a new bonus column on the DataFrame set to the salary column multiplied by two. Return the updated DataFrame.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import pandas as pd

def createBonusColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['bonus'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees
```

complexity.notes: Vectorized column multiplication and assignment in contiguous memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using apply() with a lambda or iterating with a loop introduces heavy interpreter overhead compared to vectorized Series arithmetic.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct vectorized column assignment scales linearly in O(N) time and allocates an O(N) Series.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using vectorized multiplication rather than apply(lambda x: x * 2).

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def createBonusColumn(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employees['bonus'] = employees['salary'] * 2
    return employees
